prompt.context: Your client is a private equity firm considering an investment in Howliday Inn, a national chain providing doggy daycare and boarding services.
prompt.question: Size the market for doggy daycare and boarding services in the United States. Your final answer should be a dollar figure.

clarifying_info.q: How many people are in the United States?
What is the average household size?
What percentage of households own a dog?
What is the average rate for doggy daycare?
What is the average rate for dog boarding?
Should I use a top-down or bottom-up approach?
clarifying_info.a: Either is fine; top-down is suggested if you are unsure

exhibits.title: Survey of U.S. Dog Owners – Doggy Daycare Usage
exhibits.shows: Survey results (n=10,000) showing what share of dog-owning households regularly use doggy daycare and, among those who do, how frequently they use it per week

exhibits.title: Survey of U.S. Dog Owners – Dog Boarding Usage
exhibits.shows: Survey results (n=10,000) showing what share of dog-owning households regularly use dog boarding services, plus expert commentary on typical boarding frequency and stay length

data.expert_commentary_nights_per_stay: ~2 nights per stay (Howliday Inn regional manager)

exhibits.title: Exhibit page header (n=10,000 survey)
exhibits.shows: Cover/header page for the exhibit set indicating total survey sample size

framework: Step 1 – Size the total addressable population: derive number of U.S. households and dog-owning households
Step 2 – Size the doggy daycare market: apply adoption rate, average usage frequency, days per year, and daily rate to get annual revenue
Step 3 – Size the dog boarding market: apply adoption rate, stays per year, nights per stay, and nightly rate to get annual revenue
Step 4 – Sum both markets for total market size
Step 5 – Sense-check and contextualize the number for the PE client

questions.prompt: Calculate the number of dog-owning households in the U.S.
questions.guidance: Divide total population by household size, then apply dog-ownership rate. Should arrive at ~50 million dog-owning households.

math.setup: (U.S. population / people per household) × % households owning dogs

questions.prompt: Calculate the annual doggy daycare market size.
questions.guidance: Apply Exhibit 1 data: 5% usage rate among dog-owning households, then weight average days per week by frequency distribution, annualize, and multiply by daily rate.

math.setup: dog-owning households × % using daycare × avg days/week × 52 weeks × $20/day

questions.prompt: Calculate the annual dog boarding market size.
questions.guidance: Apply Exhibit 2 data: 20% usage rate, 2 stays per year, 2 nights per stay, $40 per night. Straightforward multiplication.

math.setup: dog-owning households × % using boarding × stays/year × nights/stay × $40/night

questions.prompt: What is the total U.S. doggy daycare and boarding market size?
questions.guidance: Sum daycare and boarding. Candidate should state the number clearly and contextualize it for the PE client.

math.answer: ~$4.6 billion (true market per ASPCA is ~$5.6b including grooming, so this range is acceptable)

brainstorming.prompt: Beyond the market size calculation, what else should the private equity client consider before making an investment in Howliday Inn?

categories.name: Market Dynamics
ideas: Market growth rate – is the pet services market expanding?
Humanization of pets trend driving premium spending
Demographic tailwinds (millennial pet ownership, urban density)

categories.name: Competitive Landscape
ideas: Number and size of national competitors (e.g., PetSmart PetsHotel, Rover)
Market fragmentation – local vs. national chains
Barriers to entry and switching costs

categories.name: Revenue & Adjacencies
ideas: Veterinary partnerships or on-site vet services

categories.name: Investment Considerations
ideas: Unit economics and EBITDA margins per location
Capital requirements to scale (real estate, labor)

recommendation: The U.S. doggy daycare and boarding market is approximately $4.6 billion annually, indicating a substantial addressable market that could support a meaningful investment in a national chain like Howliday Inn.

Initial judgment: market size appears large enough to be attractive for a PE investment; however, the client should validate whether Howliday Inn holds a defensible share and whether the market is growing.
risks: High fragmentation may limit pricing power and create integration risk
Labor-intensive model with high turnover could compress margins
Market size estimate carries variability; true figure (per ASPCA) is ~$5.6b including grooming
next_steps: Assess market growth rate and future projections (5–10 year CAGR)
Analyze competitive landscape and Howliday Inn's relative market position
Evaluate unit economics, same-store sales growth, and margin profile
Explore adjacency revenue streams (grooming, training, retail) to assess revenue upside
